question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay that can override and lock config/tool/system defaults, or keep immutable baselines in conformance-only Policy/Nix surfaces?
rationale: This changes config precedence, runtime write behavior, diagnostics, and the security boundary, which cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Approve core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains mutable outside Nix mode.

options.title: Defer to hook design
options.body: Leave the issue open until related policy-hook proposals settle whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Approve core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.
